title: Barry
text: My name is Barry and I just finished my Bachelors of Science in Biology from the University of British Columbia. I was born and raised in Vancouver, so I have been here basically all my life. Prior to entering UBC’s Master of Data Science program I worked as a research assistant in an immunology lab that investigated the relationship between Epstein-Barr virus and multiple sclerosis. I am hoping to gain both foundational and technical data science skills from UBC’s Master of Data Science, allowing me to expand my data science toolkit within the context of immunology. I look forward to meeting new people and learning as much as I can in the coming year!

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
My first week’s in MDS have been great! During orientation I met so many people from so many different backgrounds in both academia and industry. One of the most fun parts of orientation was the campus scavenger hunt, where we got to split into teams to complete challenges. We got to tour all parts of campus, and we even got a little prize at the end (refer to image below)!
In my first week of official MDS classes, I learned so much in such a short time, from working in the terminal, R, python, and positron to understanding statistics and probabilities. Overall the days were long, but I was able to get all my homework done before the weekend which gave me some time to rest.
As I am entering pre-quiz week I am starting to feel a bit of the pressure but overall it has been a great few weeks, I was able to meet many people and make many friends from everywhere in the world!



Orientation day on campus.

title: About Me
text: I grew up here in Vancouver, Canada. I studied Biology at the University of British Columbia for undergraduate degree. Before entering MDS I mostly conducted multiple sclerosis research, this involved animal care, tissue staining, and microscopic imaging. A portion of my work also involved processing imaging and cell data, and finding ways to present or visualize the data.

title: About Me
text:
Why data science
Due to my background in more wet-lab research for most of my undergrad, I wanted to obtain a more dry-lab skillset. I also observed that a lot of scientific research involves a lot of data (often messy too) however many labs lack a resident data scientist to turn to. Because of this gap, I decided it would be useful for me to have a data science background and skillset if I wanted to continue working in the context of biology whether it be industry and academia.

title: About Me
text:
Outside of data science
When I am not working or on campus I like to hit up the gym with my friends or go out to eat! UBC’s Recreation North fitness centre provides a great place to workout due to large number of machines they now have. Outside of excercise I like to go out to eat and try new places around Vancouver with my friends. Other hobbies I am interested in include origami and a little bit of gaming (Overcooked 2!).
